observations: AT&T investor relations reports Q2 2026 revenue of $31.6B, adjusted EBITDA of $12.3B, free cash flow of $4.7B, 432K postpaid phone net adds and 646K Advanced Connectivity internet net adds.
The filed 10-Q shows Advanced Connectivity consumer service revenue of $18.069B, up 6.2% year over year, including advanced home internet revenue of $2.926B, up 27.3%.
Advanced Connectivity business fiber/advanced-connectivity revenue was $1.946B, up 10.0% year over year, while transitional and other service revenue declined 16.6%.
factors: legacy-network migration can shift mix toward higher-growth advanced connectivity
risks: legacy service contraction remains material during network transition
capital intensity of fiber/network expansion requires sustained cash generation
headline adjusted EBITDA/free-cash-flow metrics require reconciliation discipline versus GAAP filings
contradictions: Advanced connectivity is growing while transitional/legacy service continues to contract, so consolidated growth depends on the new platform outpacing deliberate legacy runoff.
unknowns: incremental return on capital from the expanded fiber footprint
durability of convergence-driven retention and ARPU economics across acquired fiber assets

recommendation.reason: First structured Scout pair supplies primary filed operating evidence and current execution metrics for underwriting.
